title: Atrial fibrillation phenotypes derived from multimodal data exhibit distinct electrophysiological substrate characteristics, symptom trajectories, and ablation outcomes.
summary:
AIMS: The heterogeneity in response to catheter ablation amongst atrial fibrillation (AF) patients classified according to arrhythmia duration highlights the need for improved phenotyping. Multimodal assessment may better characterize the spectrum of pathophysiology present amongst patients classified as having paroxysmal or persistent AF. This study aimed to perform comprehensive multimodal pre-ablation phenotyping in patients undergoing AF ablation and evaluate associations with post-ablation arrhythmia recurrence, symptom burden, and bi-atrial substrate remodelling.

METHODS AND RESULTS: In this multicentre prospective cohort study, 86 patients referred for first-time AF ablation (42% persistent AF) underwent pre-ablation phenotyping beyond usual care, incorporating patch-based ambulatory rhythm monitoring, atrial structural and functional MRI assessment, and formal symptom evaluation. Unsupervised K-means clustering was used to derive phenotypes. The primary outcome was 12-month arrhythmia recurrence; secondary analyses assessed symptom trajectories and bi-atrial substrate characteristics. Four AF phenotypes were identified. Arrhythmia recurrence occurred in 56.0%, 42.9%, 22.2%, and 19.0% of patients in Phenotypes 1-4, respectively (log-rank P = 0.032). Symptom trajectories differed across phenotypes, with the greatest improvements observed in Phenotypes 3 and 4. Exploratory electroanatomic mapping analyses demonstrated significant between-phenotype differences in bi-atrial bipolar voltage aligned with clinical trajectories. Importantly, phenotypes were not fully explained by conventional classification: Phenotype 2 experienced relatively high recurrence despite comprising predominantly paroxysmal AF patients whilst Phenotype 3 demonstrated favourable outcomes despite a high prevalence of persistent AF.

CONCLUSION: Multimodal phenotyping identified distinct AF subgroups associated with differences in post-ablation recurrence, symptom trajectories, and electrophysiological substrate. This approach could improve pre-ablation risk stratification and shared decision-making.

REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05057507.

title: Sex-based differences in the atrial fibrillation care pathway and outcomes: an ITHACA-database analysis.
summary:
AIMS: To characterize sex-specific differences in clinical presentation, evaluate progression through the atrial fibrillation (AF) care pathway from diagnosis to catheter ablation (CA) and assess long-term outcomes.

METHODS AND RESULTS: This was a retrospective cohort study of patients with incident AF at Northwell Health between 2015 and 2024 from the ITHACA-database. Sex-specific differences in clinical presentation were examined. The AF care pathway was operationalized as a stepwise cascade, modelling conditional drop-off to identify care gaps. Sex-specific CA risk ratios were assessed via Poisson regression. Incident AF was identified among 165 563/655 459 patients (71.4 ± 11.6 years, 32% non-white, 45% female) with a recorded diagnosis of AF. Women were older (73.3 ± 10.6 vs. 69.8 ± 12.1 years, P < 0.001), had higher rates of dementia (9.1% vs. 5.2%), stroke (8.6% vs. 7.4%) and congestive heart failure (21.5% vs. 20.8%) at diagnosis. Transfer-of-care gaps [median 3.6 years follow-up, 96% retention] were identified at every level: 31.5% of women vs. 35.3% of men were evaluated by cardiology, 16.2% vs. 21.6% by electrophysiology, and 3.5% vs. 5.7% underwent CA (all P < 0.001). Women were 16% less likely to receive CA (RR 0.84 95% CI 0.77-0.91). In cause-specific Cox models, female sex was associated with incident stroke (aHR 1.24, 95% CI 1.18-1.30) and dementia (aHR 1.30, 95% CI 1.24-1.35), but modestly lower mortality after adjustment (aHR 0.96, 95% CI 0.94-0.99).

CONCLUSION: In this real-world analysis, significant sex-specific differences in clinical phenotype at presentation, progression through the AF care pathway and clinical outcomes were observed.

title: A randomized comparison of comprehensive weight loss intervention vs. usual care on recurrences of atrial fibrillation in obese patients after catheter ablation: HOBIT-AF trial.
summary:
AIMS: Obesity is one of the strongest risk factors for the development of atrial fibrillation (AF), and its reduction is associated with the alleviation of AF burden. The HOBIT-AF study aimed to evaluate the impact of complex weight loss interventions on AF recurrence rate in obese individuals after catheter ablation (CA).

METHODS AND RESULTS: The HOBIT-AF was a randomized controlled trial with a 15-month treatment period (3-18 months post CA) involving complex weight-reducing interventions in the active arm. The primary outcome was the change in AF/atrial tachycardia (AT) burden assessed from baseline and the final 14-day Holter monitoring. A total of 167 individuals (aged 59 years, body mass index of 35.6 kg/m2) were randomized into the active (n = 85) and control group (n = 82). At the end of the treatment period, a mean reduction of 6.8 ± 7.0% of the initial body weight accompanied by improvement of metabolic parameters was achieved in the active group. The AF/AT burden change was 0.6 ± 2.5% (95% CI: -4.2-5.5%) in the active group and -0.9 ± 1.8% (95% CI: -4.5-3.0%) in the control group. The AF/AT recurrence-free survival during the 3-18-month follow-up period was comparable between groups (70.4% vs. 69.6%).

CONCLUSION: HOBIT-AF trial showed that despite the beneficial effect of body weight reduction on metabolic profile of obese patients with predominantly paroxysmal AF after CA, no reduction in AF/AT recurrence was observed in comparison with control patients. This may be likely due to low AF burden after previous CA, limiting further improvement.

title: Pulmonary Vein Anatomy, Cooling Kinetics, and Recurrence After Cryoballoon Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Cryoballoon pulmonary vein isolation depends on balloon-to-ostium contact. We assessed whether computed tomography-derived pulmonary vein ostial area (OA) and ovality index (OI) were associated with cooling after accounting for pulmonary vein (PV) branch and within-patient clustering, and whether PV anatomy was associated with recurrence.

METHODS: We retrospectively studied 120 patients with symptomatic atrial fibrillation undergoing second-generation cryoballoon ablation. Vein-level associations with nadir temperature, 1 min temperature, and time to isolation were assessed using linear mixed-effects models with a patient random intercept and PV branch as a fixed effect; generalized estimating equations served as sensitivity analyses. Given 23 post-blanking recurrences, logistic models were limited to left atrial volume index (LAVI) and one clinically selected covariate, with Firth-penalized regression as a sensitivity analysis.

RESULTS: All patients achieved acute PV isolation. Larger OA was associated with lower nadir temperature (β = -0.583°C per 50 mm2; 95% CI, -0.910 to -0.257; p < 0.001) and 1 min temperature (β = -0.441°C per 50 mm2; 95% CI, -0.764 to -0.118; p = 0.008) after branch and clustering adjustment. OI was not associated with either temperature outcome. Twenty-three patients (19.2%) developed recurrent atrial arrhythmia. LAVI was associated with recurrence (adjusted OR, 1.659 per 10 mL/m2; 95% CI, 1.250-2.201; p < 0.001), whereas persistent AF was not.

CONCLUSIONS: OA showed a modest association with cryoballoon temperatures but should not be used as a stand-alone prognostic marker. LAVI remained associated with recurrence in parsimonious patient-level analyses.

title: Commentary: Clinical Implications of Structural and Electrical Recurrence after Mitral Valve Repair and Concomitant Atrial Fibrillation Ablation.
A Pharmacist-Led Antiplatelet Therapy Stewardship Initiative in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation Receiving Concomitant Oral Anticoagulants and Single Antiplatelet Therapy.
summary: Concomitant therapy with anticoagulants and antiplatelets in patients with atrial fibrillation and chronic coronary syndrome significantly increases the risk of bleeding with no added reduction in cardiovascular disease risk over anticoagulation alone. The primary objective was to evaluate an evidence-based antiplatelet stewardship service designed to deprescribe single antiplatelet therapy in patients with atrial fibrillation receiving oral anticoagulants and a single antiplatelet therapy for both primary and secondary prevention of cardiovascular disease. This retrospective study included adult patients aged older than 18 years with atrial fibrillation who were seen at a tertiary academic heart failure center and received therapeutic oral anticoagulants and single antiplatelet therapy for any cardiovascular secondary or primary prevention. The primary outcome was the acceptance of the antiplatelet deprescribing intervention by both providers and patients. The secondary outcomes included provider- or patient-accepted antiplatelet deprescribing intervention. A total of 71 patients were included in the final cohort of this study. The most common indication for the antiplatelet therapy was chronic coronary disease at 69.0 % followed by primary prevention at 14.1% and stroke at 11.3%. The most common antiplatelet therapy was aspirin 81 mg once daily (83.1%), followed by clopidogrel 75 mg once daily(16.9%). Among the 71 patients, 54 (76.1%) were on non-guideline directed antiplatelet therapy. Of the 54 recommendations, 50 (92.6%) were accepted by the providers, and 43 of the 50 provider-accepted recommendations (86.0%) were accepted by the patients. Conclusion: A pharmacist-led antiplatelet deprescribing service is feasible in a tertiary heart failure cardiology outpatient setting. Most recommendations were accepted by the providers and patients.

title: Ebstein Anomaly With Pre-excited Atrial Fibrillation.
Emotional distress in patients before first-time and redo catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia and is frequently accompanied by anxiety and depressive symptoms, which may affect quality of life. While catheter ablation (CA) is an established therapy for AF, data comparing emotional distress burden prior to first-time vs. redo CA procedures remain limited.

AIM: To compare pre-procedural anxiety and depressive symptoms in patients undergoing first-time AF/atypical atrial flutter CA vs. those undergoing redo AF/atypical atrial flutter CA.

METHODS: This prospective observational study included patients with AF or atypical atrial flutter scheduled for CA (first-time or redo) between January 2024 and May 2025. Anxiety and depressive symptoms were assessed one day prior to the CA using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS).

RESULTS: Overall, 112 patients who underwent first-time CA and 49 patients who underwent redo CA were included. Most baseline characteristics were similar between groups; however, redo CA patients had a higher prevalence of persistent AF and prior stroke and higher CHA₂DS₂-VA scores. Patients scheduled for first-time (vs. redo) CA had significantly higher emotional distress. Median HADS depression and anxiety scores were significantly higher in the first-time CA group compared with the redo CA group (10 [9-11] vs. 2 [1-5], p < 0.001 and 13 [11.5-14] vs. 5 [2-9], p < 0.001; respectively. Distributional analyses demonstrated a consistent shift of the HADS-A and HADS-D score distributions toward higher values in the first-time CA group, supported by large non-parametric effect sizes. After adjustment for persistent AF, diabetes mellitus, and prior stroke, first-time CA remained associated with a higher burden of anxiety and depressive symptoms compared with redo CA patients. Persistent AF was associated with lower odds of depressive symptoms.

CONCLUSIONS: Patients undergoing first-time AF CA experience higher anxiety and depressive symptom burden than those undergoing redo CA.

title: Electrical storm due to ectopic activity following successful reperfusion: Clinical characterization and pharmacological approach to angry Purkinje syndrome
summary: Introduction: Angry Purkinje syndrome is an uncommon cause of electrical storm characterized by short-coupled premature ventricular complexes (PVCs) originating from the His-Purkinje system and triggering polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (PMVT) or ventricular fibrillation (VF). It may occur during the subacute phase after myocardial infarction despite successful coronary reperfusion and absence of recurrent ischemia. Case presentation: A 55-year-old man presented with persistent oppressive precordial chest pain, rated 8/10, radiating to the jaw and left arm, which had begun at 02:00 h while asleep, without associated autonomic symptoms. On admission, blood pressure was 174/101 mmHg and heart rate was 103 beats/min. Electrocardiography showed an extensive anterior myocardial infarction, and primary percutaneous coronary intervention restored TIMI 3 flow in the left anterior descending coronary artery. Seventy-two hours after complete coronary revascularization, the patient developed ventricular fibrillation requiring external defibrillation with 150 J (Figure 2E). At the time of the first arrest, serum troponin was 896 pg/mL, potassium was 4.5 mEq/L, and magnesium was 2.62 mEq/L. The heart rate was 50 beats/min, with a QTc of 413 ms. Continuous cardiac monitoring subsequently demonstrated frequent premature ventricular complexes (PVCs) with a coupling interval of approximately 380 ms and a right bundle branch block morphology with a superior axis, followed by episodes of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (PMVT) initiated by short-coupled PVCs (Figure 2A–D). Following this event, diagnostic coronary angiography was performed because of suspected acute stent thrombosis, confirming patency of the left anterior descending coronary artery stent with TIMI 3 flow and no new angiographic lesions in the remaining coronary arteries. Conclusion: Angry Purkinje syndrome should be considered in patients who develop recurrent PMVT or VF initiated by short-coupled PVCs after successful myocardial reperfusion, particularly when recurrent ischemia has been excluded. Flecainide combined with atrial overdrive pacing may represent a potential rescue strategy when quinidine is unavailable; however, further evidence is required to determine its efficacy and safety in this setting.

title: Defining the Substrate in Scar-Related Ventricular Tachycardia: A Hierarchy of Evidence for Arrhythmogenicity.
summary: Scar-related monomorphic ventricular tachycardia is sustained by a limited re-entry circuit within a much larger field of diseased myocardium. Late gadolinium enhancement cardiac magnetic resonance and cardiac computed tomography define scar distribution, channel architecture, wall thickness, and tissue composition, but cannot demonstrate conduction or circuit participation. Voltage mapping and abnormal electrograms identify electrically abnormal myocardium, although their appearance depends on activation sequence, catheter geometry, contact, and annotation. Functional mapping reveals rate-dependent slowing, decrement, and block that may be concealed during baseline rhythm. Mapping during ventricular tachycardia (VT) provides the most direct evidence of circuit participation, but is often limited by hemodynamic instability, noninducibility, or incomplete surface representation of a 3-dimensional circuit. This review examines how to weight these findings when defining the arrhythmogenic substrate. Structural imaging establishes where a circuit could reside and how it may be accessed. Baseline electroanatomic mapping characterizes the electrical expression of surviving myocardium, while functional mapping tests whether conduction deteriorates with changes in wave front or coupling interval. Activation and entrainment provide the strongest evidence that a region participates in a specific VT. These findings should be integrated hierarchically rather than by simple spatial overlap, adjusting interpretation for disease phenotype, substrate depth, mapped surface, and recording conditions. The arrhythmogenic substrate is best understood as surviving myocardium within scar whose 3-dimensional architecture and electrophysiological behavior permit re-entry. A reproducible definition will require standardized acquisition and annotation, explicit reporting of the evidence linking a region to VT, and prospective validation using mapped circuits.

title: A Novel Bundle Branch Re-Entrant Ventricular Tachycardia Using a Septal Purkinje Network as the Retrograde Limb.
Primary Prevention ICD in a Contemporary Underserved Population: Factors Associated With Underutilization and Mortality.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Registry studies from 2000-2010 demonstrated underutilization of primary prevention ICD therapy. As heart failure therapies have reduced sudden cardiac death, investigators have questioned guidelines derived from trials conducted two decades prior, particularly in non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) and elderly subgroups. We characterized contemporary referral determinants, decision-making processes, and outcomes of primary prevention ICD therapy in a diverse, under-represented population.

METHODS: In this retrospective single-center cohort study, we reviewed records of all patients meeting Class I criteria for primary prevention ICD in 2019. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with ICD referral, and time-varying Cox models compared all-cause mortality by implantation status through 2022.

RESULTS: Of 559 eligible patients, 345 (62%) were referred and 227 (41%) underwent implantation. Referral was associated with male gender, care coordination by a cardiologist rather than a generalist, and lower social vulnerability index (SVI) score. No decision-making rationale was documented for a plurality of non-referred and non-implanted patients; documented rationales identified potential intervention targets. ICD implantation was not associated with all-cause mortality (aHR 0.74, 95% CI 0.49-1.12). In exploratory analyses stratified by cardiomyopathy type, implantation was associated with lower mortality in ischemic cardiomyopathy (aHR 0.51, 95% CI 0.27-0.95) but not in NICM (aHR 1.11, 95% CI 0.63-1.95).

CONCLUSION: Many eligible patients are never referred for ICD therapy. Female gender, generalist care coordination, and high SVI were associated with non-referral. The exploratory association of implantation with lower mortality in ischemic cardiomyopathy was not significant in propensity score overlap-weighted analyses. The NICM estimate was imprecise.

title: VDD Pacemaker Implantation Without Fluoroscopy for Complete Heart Block During Pregnancy: A Case Report.
summary: Ionizing radiation is associated with an increased risk of malignancy, especially in fetuses. Therefore, in the rare situation of a pregnant patient in need of a pacemaker, alternatives to conventional fluoroscopy are required. We describe a case of successful implantation of a Ventricle-paced, Dual-sensing, Dual-response pacemaker without fluoroscopy in a 32-year-old female patient using electroanatomic 3D mapping. She had severe bradycardia due to complete atrioventricular block, which impeded intrauterine growth restriction in the fetus.

title: Age-stratified clinical phenotypes of cardiac implantable electronic device infections: a 20-year retrospective cohort study.
summary:
BACKGROUND: The widespread adoption of cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) has been accompanied by a parallel increase in severe CIED infections. Traditional risk stratification frequently relies on binary age cutoffs, which can obscure how infection phenotypes evolve across a patient's lifespan. This study evaluated how advancing age-analyzed across ordered chronological strata-correlates with anatomical infection site, device hardware type, microbiology, and in-hospital mortality in patients with CIED infections.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study of 383 patients treated for CIED infections between 2002 and 2022, patients were categorized into five sequential age brackets (< 50 to 80-90 years). Age was modeled both categorically across these strata and continuously to estimate per-decade odds ratios (ORs) for clinical presentation, hardware type, and microbiological findings.

RESULTS: The cohort was predominantly male (75.2%) with a mean age of 67.4 years. Pacemaker involvement increased significantly with age (p < 0.001), whereas implantable cardioverter-defibrillator use declined (p = 0.036). Localized generator pocket infections demonstrated a pronounced age-dependent gradient, rising from 19.4% in patients under 50 years to 73.0% in octogenarians (p < 0.001; OR 1.43 per decade, 95% CI: 1.21-1.69). Conversely, systemic presentations-including bacteremia and lead endocarditis-showed no age-dependent trend. In-hospital mortality remained low and stable across age groups (p = 0.452) but was markedly higher in patients presenting with bacteremia or sepsis compared to those without systemic involvement (16.7% vs. 1.6%, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Analyzing age as a continuous spectrum reveals a distinct clinical phenotype dominated by localized pocket infections and low-power devices, an insight obscured by standard binary age cutoffs. Crucially, mortality risk was driven by systemic bloodstream infection rather than patient age itself, emphasizing that clinical surveillance should prioritize infection phenotype over chronological age alone.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

title: Bachmann Bundle Pacing and Acute Changes in Left Atrial Mechanical Function in Patients With Interatrial Block: A Within-Subject Echocardiography Analysis.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Interatrial block (IAB) is associated with atrial electromechanical dysfunction and adverse cardiovascular outcomes. Bachmann bundle pacing (BBP) has emerged as a physiological atrial pacing strategy capable of restoring interatrial conduction synchrony. However, its impact on left atrial (LA) mechanical function and hemodynamics remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the acute effects of BBP on atrial mechanical parameters in patients with IAB.

METHODS: In this prospective single-center study, 31 patients with IAB who underwent successful BBP implantation were enrolled. A standardized postoperative evaluation protocol was performed under intrinsic sinus rhythm (SR), right atrial septal pacing (RASP) at atrial lead threshold +0.5 V/0.4 ms, and BBP at 5 V/0.4 ms using a within-subject repeated-measures design. Electrocardiographic and echocardiographic parameters were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models, with additional adjustment for heart rate.

RESULTS: BBP produced significantly greater P wave duration (PWD) shortening than RASP (p < 0.001). Compared with SR, BBP was associated with lower LA volume indices and higher LA emptying fraction and LA expansion index (all p < 0.001), with consistent superiority over RASP at acute postoperative phase. These associations remained significant after heart rate adjustment. The observed acute changes were consistent across partial and advanced IAB subgroups without significant interaction effects.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with IAB, electrical resynchronization during BBP was accompanied by acute changes in LA mechanical parameters compared with SR and RASP. These findings suggest that BBP may represent a promising physiological pacing strategy for patients with atrial conduction disease.

title: hiPSC-derived new approach methodology (NAM) recapitulates hallmarks of atrial fibrillation.
summary:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Human in vitro models for atrial fibrillation (AF) remain limited in reproducing disease-specific remodeling. We leveraged a human-induced pluripotent stem cell-derived atrial cardiomyocyte (hiPSC-aCM) model, which was co-cultured with human atrial cardiac fibroblasts (haCFs) and subjected to an intermittent tachypacing protocol (ITPP) to mimic AF-associated phenotypes.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Human iPSC-derived atrial cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-aCMs) were differentiated, purified, matured, and cultured alone or co-cultured with human atrial cardiac fibroblasts at defined seeding ratios (e.g., 90/10 or 70/30 hiPSC-aCM/haCF). Cultures were subjected to 7 days of intermittent tachypacing using electrical field stimulation. Functional electrophysiology and calcium handling were assessed by high-throughput optical mapping, arrhythmia inducibility testing, and genetically encoded or chemical calcium indicators. Structural and molecular remodeling were evaluated by immunocytochemistry, qPCR, and Western blot analysis.

RESULTS: ITPP increased spontaneous action potential (AP) frequency and shortened AP duration at 80% repolarization (APD80%), while reducing calcium transient (CaT) upstroke slope and amplitude. Co-cultures at a 70/30 hiPSC-aCM/haCF ratio exhibited marked structural remodeling, with a >100-fold increase in Collagen III expression (P < 0.0001), decreased excitability (ΔHz = -61 ± 6%, P < 0.0001), prolonged APD80% (Δ = +130 ± 10%, P < 0.0001), increased triangulation (ΔAPDTri = +143 ± 13%, P < 0.0001), reduced upstroke slope (Δ = -66 ± 6%, P < 0.0001), conduction block (Δ = -52 ± 18%, P = 0.026), and impaired Ca2⁺ handling (upstroke slope Δ = -50 ± 8%, P < 0.0001; ΔdF/F0 = -34 ± 9%, P = 0.0003). Applying ITPP to the 70/30 co-culture induced AF-like remodeling, with increased spontaneous activity (ΔHz = +25 ± 8%, P = 0.02), shortened APD80% (Δ = -16 ± 6%, P = 0.01), and reduced conduction velocity (ΔCV100/0 vs. 70/30 = -27 ± 15%, P = 0.0005). Mechanistically, ITPP led to downregulation of phospholamban (PLN) and altered PLN-SERCA2a balance, along with upregulation of TGFB1 and natriuretic peptides, reflecting calcium-handling dysfunction and pro-fibrotic signaling.

CONCLUSION: Together, these findings establish a human-relevant platform in 2D culture that recapitulates key AF-associated structural and electrophysiological remodeling for mechanistic studies and therapeutic screening.

title: Complex antiarrhythmic effects of empagliflozin in non-ischemic HFrEF cardiomyocytes.
summary:
INTRODUCTION: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors improve clinical outcomes in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and may reduce sudden cardiac death; however, the underlying antiarrhythmic mechanisms remain incompletely understood.

METHODS: We investigated the cellular electrophysiological effects of the SGLT2 inhibitor empagliflozin in isolated cardiomyocytes from two non-ischemic, non-diabetic HFrEF models (rabbit and mouse).

RESULTS: Ventricular cardiomyocytes from both HFrEF models exhibited prolonged action potential duration (APD), increased short-term APD variability (STV), and greater susceptibility to APD alternans and delayed afterdepolarizations (DADs). Intracellular Ca2+ buffering with EGTA prevented DADs, attenuated APD prolongation, and reduced repolarization instability. HFrEF cardiomyocytes also showed enhanced late Na+ current (INa,L) and reduced inward rectifier K+ current (IK1). Cell pretreatment with empagliflozin (1 μmol/L, 3 h), but not acute application (3 min), attenuated proarrhythmogenic AP changes, reduced INa,L, and increased IK1 in both species. Empagliflozin had no significant electrophysiological effects in healthy control cardiomyocytes. Selective inhibition of Na+/H+ exchanger-1 (NHE-1) with cariporide (1 μmol/L, 3 h) failed to reproduce the antiarrhythmic effects of empagliflozin under our experimental conditions; however, our studies were performed with intracellular pH buffered to 7.2, where NHE-1 activity is low.

DISCUSSION: These results demonstrate that empagliflozin attenuates key proarrhythmic electrophysiological changes in non-ischemic HFrEF cardiomyocytes. The requirement for drug pretreatment supports the hypothesis that empagliflozin acts through modulation of ion channel functional expression and/or post-translational regulation rather than direct acute channel effects in non-ischemic HFrEF cardiomyocytes.

title: Acute mechanical stretch enhances β-adrenergic-protein kinase A signalling and increases susceptibility to ventricular arrhythmias.
summary: Mechanical stretch can increase ventricular arrhythmia susceptibility during sympathetic activation, but the mechanisms linking stretch to altered β-adrenergic receptor (βAR) signalling, Ca2 + handling and electrical instability remain unclear. We tested whether left ventricular (LV) stretch alters Cav3-associated membrane organisation and enhances βAR-protein kinase A (PKA)-dependent arrhythmogenic signalling. Langendorff-perfused male rat hearts were studied using a fluid-filled LV balloon, with sham hearts fitted with an unstretched balloon. Optical mapping during S1-S2 programmed stimulation showed that LV stretch had limited effects at baseline but altered the response to βAR stimulation, increasing ventricular arrhythmia severity, prolonging APD50, reducing local conduction velocity and steepening APD80 restitution. H89 markedly reduced βAR stimulation-induced arrhythmia severity in stretched hearts, whereas KN93 did not provide comparable protection. LV stretch also increased cardiomyocyte length and altered Cav3 organisation at wheat germ agglutinin (WGA)-defined membrane regions. In isolated LV cardiomyocytes, hypoosmotic membrane deformation did not alter basal caffeine-induced Ca2 + release but enhanced isoprenaline-induced irregular activity and Ca2 +-transient amplitude, both of which were attenuated by PKA inhibition. Hypoosmotic membrane deformation also amplified isoprenaline-evoked PKA activity and increased RyR2 Ser2030 phosphorylation. These findings indicate that LV mechanical stretch alters the ventricular βAR response in association with altered Cav3-associated membrane organisation and enhanced βAR-PKA-dependent Ca2 + instability. KEY POINTS: Left ventricular (LV) balloon stretch has limited baseline electrophysiological effects but increases arrhythmia severity, slows conduction and steepens APD80 restitution during β-adrenergic stimulation. LV balloon stretch is associated with cardiomyocyte elongation and altered Cav3 enrichment at wheat germ agglutinin (WGA)-defined membrane regions. Hypoosmotic membrane deformation enhances isoprenaline-induced irregular activity and Ca2 +-transient amplitude without increasing basal caffeine-induced Ca2 + release. PKA inhibition reduces stretch-enhanced irregular activity in isolated ventricular myocytes and β-adrenergic receptor (βAR)-induced arrhythmia severity in stretched hearts. Hypoosmotic membrane deformation enhances isoprenaline-evoked PKA activity and increases RyR2 Ser2030 phosphorylation.

title: Isoproterenol for Bradycardia Associated Prolonged QT Interval After Mixed Drug Overdose.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Prolonged QT interval is a marker for risk of ventricular arrhythmias. Risk factors include medications, bradycardia, female sex, genetics, advanced age, structural abnormalities, and electrolyte derangements.

CASE SUMMARY: This case describes an 18-year-old woman with an extensive psychiatric history who overdosed on escitalopram and guanfacine in a suicide attempt. At 33 hours from ingestion, QTc interval measured 658 milliseconds with persistent bradycardia. Isoproterenol successfully prevented emergence of torsades de pointes (TdP).

DISCUSSION: Coingestion of substances in the setting of overdose requires prompt identification of toxidromes in anticipation of potential complications. Management for prolonged QTc interval should be based on TdP risk assessment considering patient and clinical factors.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: In select hospitalized patients with sinus bradycardia at high risk for TdP, early use of isoproterenol may be used to prevent the occurrence of adverse cardiac events.

title: Safety of Bioelectric Impedance Analysis Testing in Pediatric Patients With Cardiac Implantable Electronic Devices.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Bioelectric impedance analysis (BIA) is a useful clinical tool in pediatric heart disease, but concerns regarding cardiac implanted electronic devices (CIEDs) limit its use. This study's goal was to assess the impact of BIA on CIED settings in pediatric patients.

METHODS: This single-center cohort study included two groups: a retrospective cohort of patients under 21 years old who had CIED interrogation within 12 months before and after BIA use, and a smaller prospective cohort who had CIED interrogation immediately before and after BIA use. The prospective group also underwent real-time monitoring for electrical interference during BIA. Exclusion criteria included age, implanted loop recorders, and incomplete data. Analysis used either a paired t-test or a Wilcoxon signed-rank test as appropriate, with p-value < 0.05 considered statistically significant.

RESULTS: The retrospective cohort included 55 patients with 80 total tests. A statistically but not clinically significant difference in lead impedance was observed (513 [456, 627] v 513 [399, 593] ohms, p < 0.0001), though no differences were found in electrogram amplitudes, thresholds, or programmed output. When patients with multiple tests were analyzed, there remained a statistically significant difference in lead impedance (513 [399, 614] v 513 [375, 592] ohms, p = 0.0002) but not in other CIED parameters. In the prospective cohort (n = 10), no electrical interference was appreciated during BIA, and there were no before-and-after differences in CIED sensing amplitudes. No inappropriate shocks or premature device failures occurred.

CONCLUSIONS: BIA was not associated with adverse events or meaningful changes in CIED function in this pediatric cohort.
